citation.title: Real-time measurement and feedback control of ion temperature profile and toroidal rotation using fast CXRS system in JT-60U
citation.authors: M. Yoshida, Y. Sakamoto, M. Sueoka, Y. Kawamata, N. Oyama, T. Suzuki, Y. Kamada, the JT-60 Team
citation.doi_or_arxiv: 10.1016/j.fusengdes.2009.04.006 (this paper's own DOI, from the p.1 footer)

scope_read.limitations: Figures were read from the rendered pages. The values discussed below were legible.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: Charge-exchange Ti has been used as a real-time feedback-controlled quantity. The controlled quantity was a Ti gradient over r/a ~0.25-0.5.
claim_checks.source_finding: The controlled quantity, grad-Ti, is the Ti difference between two chords. It was r/a~0.25 minus 0.5 under PD and PID control, and r/a~0.3 minus 0.55 under Ti-dependent proportional gain. The actuator was the number of NB units. A separate loop controlled Vt at r/a~0.27.
claim_checks.locator: p.4 Sec 4.1, Eqs.1-2; p.5 Fig.7; p.6 Fig.8; p.7 Sec 4.2, Fig.10; p.7 Sec 4.3, Eq.3, Fig.11
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: Carbon CXRS ion temperature has been used directly in closed-loop control on JT-60U. There, neutral-beam power regulated a two-chord core Ti difference, which served as a proxy for internal transport barrier strength.
claim_checks.qualification: This was JT-60U, not KSTAR. The control was core-region and two-point, not profile control. The source's own CX measurement was the feedback signal, not an estimate.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: Cycle time and number of radial points.
claim_checks.source_finding: The CCD frame time was 2.5 ms, with 30 chords per frame. Four selectable chords were fitted (Levenberg-Marquardt Gaussian) within 10 ms. The control loop ran every 10 ms, and the time chart places the NB command in the following cycle. A 50 ms low-pass filter was applied to Ti. Real-time Ti came out about 5% below offline Ti.
claim_checks.locator: p.2 Secs 1-2; p.3 Sec 3; p.4 Fig.4; p.5 Fig.5 and Sec 4.1 text
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: In that system, spectra were acquired every 2.5 ms, and Ti and Vt at four chords were fitted within a 10 ms control cycle. This shows that control use places explicit latency requirements on CX-derived quantities.
claim_checks.qualification: The real-time agreement check was made against the offline fit of the same spectra, not against independent truth. Report arrival latency was not separately characterized.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: An edge/pedestal chord was used for control.
claim_checks.source_finding: No edge or pedestal chord was used for control; all controlled points were at r/a≤0.55. Pedestal Ti stayed roughly constant during ITB control. Vt at r/a~0.9 and the D-alpha ELM traces were shown only as consequences of core Vt control. The authors state that Vt profile control was not yet demonstrated.
claim_checks.locator: p.6 Fig.8e and Sec 4.1 text; p.7-8 Sec 4.3, Fig.12
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: In the same work, edge rotation and ELM behaviour changed when core rotation was controlled, but the edge itself was not a controlled channel.
claim_checks.qualification: Do not cite this paper as precedent for pedestal-top CES control or estimation.

input_target_timing.inputs: CVI 529.05 nm spectra from on-beam chords, with an off-beam chord for background subtraction and a Sm lamp for wavelength reference
input_target_timing.outputs: Ti and Vt at 4 chords, fed to PID logic that sets the number of NB units
input_target_timing.causal_or_offline: Causal real-time measurement and control, plus offline 30-chord reanalysis
input_target_timing.source_diagnostic_as_input: Yes. The CX spectrum itself is the input. No BES/ECEI and no temporal nowcasting were used.
input_target_timing.reported_vs_physical_truth: Real-time fit compared with offline fit of the same spectra. The stated error is ~5%.

validation: not_applicable (this is a diagnostic and control paper, not an estimator paper)

runtime_or_deployment.what_was_measured: Real-time fitting of 4 spectra within 10 ms on a 2-CPU PC, a 10 ms control loop, and closed-loop discharges E48179, E48182, E48944 and E47806
runtime_or_deployment.what_not_established: Any relevance to KSTAR, to pedestal-top chords, or to report-availability delays in our setting. Gain generality is also not established: the authors note that gains need per-plasma optimization.
runtime_or_deployment.locator: p.3 Sec 3; p.5 Fig.5; p.5-7 Figs.7,8,10,11; p.8 Sec 4.3 end

forbidden_inferences: That this paper motivates or validates nowcasting of CES reports
That pedestal or edge Ti was controlled or measured in real time for control
That the ~5% real-time vs offline difference is accuracy against physical truth
That the method transfers to KSTAR
Citing [11-14,25] as noncausal or electron-only work
competing_or_complementary: Complementary. Faster upstream CX acquisition and fitting is an alternative route to timeliness, and it can reduce the marginal need for downstream nowcasting. Introduction framing: control use creates a latency requirement, which can be met by faster spectral readers and/or by a nowcast that estimates the current report before it arrives. The actual benefit of the latter requires validation.
